official_sources.title: Python exact stored-float representations
official_sources.finding: Python float.as_integer_ratio() returns an exact reduced rational for a finite float, while float.hex() and float.fromhex() provide an exact hexadecimal representation and round trip of the stored binary value.
official_sources.limitation: These encodings identify the stored binary float only; they do not prove source measurement accuracy, vertical datum, or that earlier decoding and unit conversion were correct.

official_sources.title: Python accurate floating-point summation
official_sources.finding: math.fsum tracks multiple intermediate partial sums to avoid precision loss, while its documentation notes dependence on IEEE-754 guarantees and a rare least-significant-bit double-rounding variation on some non-Windows builds.
official_sources.limitation: fsum improves summation accuracy but does not make unordered input canonical and is not a substitute for exact min/max enumeration or immutable input identity.

official_sources.title: Python explicit closeness and signed-zero handling
official_sources.finding: math.isclose defines a symmetric maximum-of-relative-and-absolute tolerance rule, requires a positive absolute tolerance for comparisons to zero, treats NaN as close to nothing and infinities only as close to themselves; math.copysign can expose the sign of negative zero.
official_sources.limitation: Tolerance values remain application decisions and cannot be chosen from displayed decimal digits alone.

official_sources.title: NumPy sum accumulator, overflow and reduction precision
official_sources.finding: NumPy sum uses the selected accumulator dtype, performs modular integer arithmetic without raising overflow, and may use partial pairwise floating summation depending on axis and memory layout, so exact precision can vary with parameters.
official_sources.limitation: A faster or more accurate reduction is not necessarily bitwise invariant across dtype, shape, axis, memory layout, NumPy version, or CPU implementation.

official_sources.title: NumPy allclose asymmetry and small-value warning
official_sources.finding: NumPy allclose uses abs(a-b) <= atol + rtol*abs(b), which is asymmetric; its default absolute tolerance is unsuitable for values much smaller than one, and equal_nan can deliberately treat colocated NaNs as equal.
official_sources.limitation: Passing allclose does not prove identical cell support, bit patterns, signed-zero provenance, units, or source lineage.

official_sources.title: NumPy floating-point exception policy
official_sources.finding: NumPy seterr controls divide-by-zero, overflow, underflow and invalid-operation handling and can raise FloatingPointError; integer scalar operations are also affected by these settings.
official_sources.limitation: Exception policy must be set and recorded in every worker or context; it cannot detect semantically wrong but finite values.

official_sources.title: NumPy rounding algorithm and inexact decimal scaling
official_sources.finding: NumPy round uses nearest-even ties but documents a fast sometimes-inexact floating algorithm caused by binary decimal-fraction representation and scaling by powers of ten.
official_sources.limitation: Rounded display values cannot be fed back into extrema, differences, tolerance checks or digests without changing the computation.

official_sources.title: Python Decimal contexts, traps and exactness signals
official_sources.finding: Python Decimal provides explicit precision and rounding contexts, ROUND_HALF_EVEN, sticky flags and traps for Inexact, Rounded, Overflow and InvalidOperation, plus FloatOperation controls for mixed float/decimal use.
official_sources.limitation: Decimal arithmetic can still round when context precision is insufficient; construction from a binary float exactly preserves that float's artifact rather than the intended decimal source text.
